source.title: PROC-PORTFOLIO-001: resilient multi-supplier procurement and allocation frontier
source.body:
## Purpose

Extend capability-first sourcing beyond ranking individual offers into selecting a **feasible portfolio of allocations** across suppliers. This is a research/reference contract and implementation plan; it is not a live procurement or spend-authority change.

## Why this is the next paradigm shift

- [#5072](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/5072) evaluates individual offers and returns a Pareto frontier over landed cost, arrival and a version-bound risk measure.
- [#4901](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/issues/4901) / [#4902](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/4902) provide an effects-disabled logistics twin and conflict/reconciliation constraints.
- [#4814](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/issues/4814) describes the critical production/input-output/dependency network; [#4806](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/issues/4806) covers concentration and structural dependency; [#2977](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/issues/2977) owns public-procurement integrity evidence.
- Avoid duplicating the product/component/substitution ontology, identity, stock authority, logistics event model, public-contracting model or payment execution.

## Core shift

Best individual offer does not necessarily mean best procurement portfolio.

Model a request as units of a versioned capability to be fulfilled under hard constraints. The evaluator may split quantity across offers when allowed, but must conserve demand and never allocate beyond qualified capacity. It should compare whole portfolios—not only offers—across landed cost, service timing, shortage under declared disruption scenarios, supplier/site/critical-subtier concentration, and evidenced lifecycle/circularity impact. Keep conflicting objectives visible; no universal hidden weighted score or arbitrary winner.

### Integration seam discovered

The current single-offer evaluator in #5072 also rejects offers whose available quantity is below the full request. That is correct for single-source qualification, but would falsely exclude a partial-capacity supplier from split-award portfolios. Before a portfolio optimizer consumes its outputs, separate shared evidence/credential/capability qualification from allocation-specific quantity, capacity, landed-cost and deadline checks. Preserve the current single-source behavior until differential tests cover both modes.

## Contract requirements

1. Reuse #5072's eligibility and evidence-gating semantics. A portfolio planner must not upgrade unverified or stale offers into eligible capacity.
2. Introduce explicit, versioned allocation policy: split allowed/forbidden, minimum/maximum lot, supplier share cap, single-source exceptions, minimum independent-source count, delivery window and partial-fill behavior.
3. Distinguish nominal supplier identities from demonstrated independence. Separate names alone do not prove independent ownership, manufacturing site, critical sub-tier, geography or route. Unknown dependency links remain unknown, not zero risk.
4. Model capacity and availability observations with their own observation time, validity bounds, source provenance and credential/source status. Preserve units, currency, and exact policy/model identities.
5. Include deterministic scenario-based resilience. Report fulfilled, delayed and unfulfilled units by scenario; distinguish measured probability distributions from illustrative synthetic scenarios.
6. Preserve all non-dominated feasible portfolios or use an explicitly versioned policy to narrow them. Return explanation/constraint records; never infer purchasing authority from ranking.
7. Record local repair/reuse/refurbish alternatives and lifecycle impacts only where supported by reviewed evidence. Missing impact data is unknown, not zero.
8. Mycelix owns authority and records; Symthaea may produce advisory forecasts/scenarios; Sol-Atlas provides spatial/dependency projections; Symtropy evaluates bounded physical/operational counterfactuals. None of the advisory layers commits orders or money.
9. Design open mappings to ValueFlows intent/commitment/claim/event distinctions, GS1 EPCIS/CBV visibility events, and OCDS public-contracting lifecycle data. Standards are interoperability profiles, not proof of source truth or legal compliance.

## Independent verification and acceptance

- An independent small-instance exhaustive oracle checks every feasible allocation/portfolio for low supplier counts; it must not share the production optimizer's selection logic.
- Property tests verify quantity conservation, per-offer capacity, min-lot rules, budget limits, eligibility, deterministic canonical output, duplicate-event idempotency and no accidental winner on exact ties.
- A frozen adversarial corpus includes phantom capacity, same-parent suppliers, common-site and common-route concentration, correlated disruptions, stale capacity, incompatible units, invalid substitutions, forced partial-fill ambiguity, and misleading/missing lifecycle data.
- Any prohibited allocation or unauthorized state promotion is a hard failure; never average safety failures against cost or speed.
- Every report binds input/manifest digest, request/profile version, solver/evaluator identity, scenario set, evidence references and source SHA. Queued/pending/absent CI is not PASS evidence.
- Compare against named baselines: cheapest feasible single source, naive equal split, policy-constrained greedy allocation, and exhaustive optimum on tractable instances.
- Measure cost regret, service/shortage regret, tail shortage by scenario, supplier/site/sub-tier concentration, repair/reuse rate where evidenced, Pareto set size, runtime, memory and infeasible-request rate. Proposed numeric targets remain hypotheses until measured.

## Implementation begun

- [Draft PR #5089](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/5089) freezes the portfolio contract and benchmark requirements.
- [Draft PR #5099](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/5099) adds a bounded exact Rust reference allocator, partial-capacity split sourcing, freshness gates, shared capacity-pool accounting, independent-source constraints, named disruption scenarios, and focused tests.
- Current implementation is a small exact enumerator, capped at 16 offers / 500,000 search nodes / 2,000 feasible portfolios. These are safety bounds for the prototype, not scale claims.
- Rust could not be executed in the current authoring environment because rustc/cargo are unavailable. Tests are authored, not observed passing. Exact-head CI and independent review remain required; no queued/pending job counts as PASS.

## Phasing

S1: freeze contract, schemas, deterministic small scenarios and independent oracle.
S2: implement bounded exact portfolio enumeration for small instances; compare to oracle.
S3: add a deterministic scalable heuristic only after exact-oracle agreement; report optimality gap where known and never label heuristic output as optimal.
S4: integrate synthetic scenarios with #4902; then separately qualify any shadow/pilot integration.

## Scope limits

No live supplier scraping, product equivalence inference by an LLM, actual RFQs/orders, spending, payment, real stock mutations, or operational route dispatch. Civilian-first cases: maintenance supplies, repairable IT equipment, food essentials and community infrastructure.

## Research references

- [Capability-first sourcing PR #5072](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/5072)
- [LOG-COMMONS architecture #4900](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/issues/4900)
- [GS1 EPCIS/CBV](https://www.gs1.org/standards/epcis)
- [Open Contracting Data Standard](https://www.open-contracting.org/data-standard/)
- [ISO 20400 sustainable procurement guidance](https://www.iso.org/standard/63026.html)
- [ValueFlows specification](https://www.valueflo.ws/specification/vfspec/)
